coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 7 units (the domain directory itself plus 12.01–12.06), 39 .md files — exactly matching the expected counts. Every file was read. For the eleven largest feature files (12.01.01–12.01.04, 12.02.01–12.02.03, 12.03.01–12.03.02, 12.04.01, 12.07) the '## Deep Think Annotations' sections were read selectively rather than line-by-line; all Overview / Role Lens / Behavior / Happy Path / Edge Cases / States / Decisions / Open Questions / Cross-Cut content was read in full, and every DT-NN referenced by a finding was checked in place. Rubric dimensions 1 (Problem Clarity), 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are N/A for every unit: they are owned by meta/problem-statement.md, meta/personas.md, meta/constraints.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md, which lie outside this domain and are referenced-never-redefined by these files (explicit in release-distribution-index.md:84, 'Personas are defined in meta/personas.md — referenced only, never redefined here'). Applicable checkpoints per unit are therefore dimensions 3, 5, 7 and 8.

findings.claim: The validation rule pack is simultaneously specified as pinned at gate-green (with dispatch held if it moves) and as not pinned until hand-off to the DDEX layer (with an immediate store-scoped fallback to Blocked). The two produce different artist-facing behaviour and different delivery outcomes, and 12.01.03 contradicts itself on the same page.
findings.evidence: 12.01.03-delivery-readiness-gate.md:178 'When the gate reaches `Ready` it **pins the version of every fact it was green against**:' and :184 '| Validation rule pack | 12.01.02 D-02 — rule packs are versioned data |', with :114 '| E-2 | A pinned evidence version moved between gate-green and dispatch | **Re-evaluate · hold dispatch if now unmet** |'. Against 12.01.02-metadata-validation-conformance.md:129 '| Gate-green, awaiting scheduled delivery | Current, live — validation is **not** pinned yet | The release falls back to Blocked **on the affected store only**; the artist is notified' and :130 '| At hand-off to the DDEX layer (12.02.01 requests the profile) | **Pinned** — to the same partner-knowledge-store version the profile pins to (12.02.02 D-02) |'. 12.01.03 also contradicts its own pin table at :235 'Rule pack updates between green and dispatch | P-1 is a **precondition**, not a condition — a rule-pack regression un-presents the gate rather than failing it. The release falls back to validation and says why'. Corroborated against 12.02.01-ern-message-generation.md D-11 ('The profile is **pinned at generation start** (the delivery window), not at scheduling') and 12.02.02-per-partner-profile-conformance.md D-02 ('pins together with validation at hand-off to one version number').
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a rule-pack update landing between gate-green and dispatch (a) is absorbed because the gate pinned the pack, (b) fires E-2 and produces `Held at dispatch`, or (c) un-presents the gate immediately, drops the release back to validation on the affected store only, notifies the artist, and delivers that store late past its lead-time cutoff. All three are stated in the tree; an implementer must pick one.
findings.notes: The three answers are not cosmetic: (c) notifies the artist days early and ships the other stores on schedule; (b) says nothing until dispatch and then holds; (a) says nothing at all.

findings.claim: Whether a Tier-B store's artist ID is emitted in the delivery is answered three different ways in one file. A Tier-B store is defined as having no claim/verify path, so a Tier-B link can never become verified — which makes D-05's 'only verified IDs are emitted' equivalent to 'Tier-B stores always fall back to name-matching', the exact failure the feature exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: 12.03.04-artist-profile-linking-disambiguation.md:60 '| B — addressable, not claimable | Store accepts an artist ID in the ERN but has no self-serve claim/verify path | The ID can be emitted and held, but ownership is **asserted, not proven** — see D-05 |'. Against :135 '| D-05 | Links are typed **verified** (Tier-A claim/auth) vs **asserted** (Tier-B); only verified IDs are emitted for delivery, asserted-but-unverifiable links are flagged to Trust & Safety (24) |' and :88 'Tier-A links must be verified (D-05), Tier-B unverifiable links are flagged to Trust & Safety (24) and not used for delivery' with the state at :101 '| Unverified | A Tier-A link was asserted but not claimed | "Claim this page to use it for delivery" — not emitted until verified |'. And against Q-04, which re-opens what D-05 decided: 'For a Tier-B store (addressable, not claimable), what is the acceptable evidence bar before an asserted link is treated as trusted enough to emit — or are Tier-B links always emitted-with-warning?'
findings.forcedInvention: For every Tier-B partner, whether the ERN carries the stored artist ID (accepting an unprovable assertion) or omits it and lets the store name-match. The consequence is 12.03.04's own headline failure — 'a green board and zero streams, because the work went to someone else's discography' (:17-18).
findings.notes: Q-04 is properly owned and targeted, but it asks a question D-05 has already answered in the opposite direction; a ratified decision and an open question cannot both stand.

findings.claim: The `Held` delivery state — the state every partner suspension, credential lapse and partner outage produces — has no state in the artist-facing per-store board vocabulary, and the spec says so itself. A grep across all 39 files finds `Held` only inside 12.02.03; 12.03.02's state vocabulary, legal-transition table and territory values contain nothing for it.
findings.evidence: 12.02.03-delivery-choreography-acknowledgement.md:302 '| Held | Partner suspended, endpoint down, or our credential lapsed | **no equivalent — gap** | "Held, not lost" + honest attribution (D-06) |' and :335 'this feature\'s `Failed` and `Held` states have **no equivalent** in 12.03.02\'s board vocabulary — a credential lapse currently has nowhere honest to land'. 12.03.02-per-store-delivery-status.md:44-55 enumerates the vocabulary as Queued / Sent / Received / Accepted / Live (pre-order) / Live / Rejected / Withdrawn / Removed by store / Unknown, and its legal-transition table resolves the sibling case explicitly at :110 'Transport failure is not a state here — it is 12.02.03\'s `Failed` and stays `Sent` on the board until it resolves or ages into `Sent · overdue`' — while saying nothing about a suspension hold. 12.02.02-per-partner-profile-conformance.md:270 and :317 route the case here: 'queued releases **held, not failed**' / 'Artist: store unavailable in 12.03.01 **with a reason**; releases held, not failed'.
findings.forcedInvention: What the per-store board — 'the screen an artist actually opens during a release, and the one they judge the whole product by' (12.03-index:22-23) — renders when a partner is suspended: `Queued`, `Sent`, `Unknown`, or a new state. `Sent` over-claims (nothing was sent), `Queued` loses the reason, `Unknown` blames the partner for our credential lapse and contradicts D-06's honest-attribution rule.
findings.notes: The other two gaps this note declares have since been closed on the 12.03.02 side (see #004); `Held` was not, and no open question in either file owns it.

findings.claim: 12.02.03's state table still declares `Partially accepted` and `Failed` to have 'no equivalent — gap' on the board, but 12.03.02 has since specified a projection for both. Both statements cannot be true, and neither side carries a marker.
findings.evidence: 12.02.03-delivery-choreography-acknowledgement.md:298 '| Partially accepted | Ack: `partially-accepted` (DT-07) | **no equivalent — gap** |' and :301 '| Failed | Transport failed after the architecture\'s retry policy | **no equivalent — gap** |'. Against 12.03.02-per-store-delivery-status.md:70 'The parent projects `Partial acceptance` while evidence remains mixed' (ratified as D-18, 'Owner ratification for A-05 / `r-54[1]`, 2026-07-20') and :110 'Transport failure is not a state here — it is 12.02.03\'s `Failed` and stays `Sent` on the board until it resolves or ages into `Sent · overdue`'. 12.02-ddex-delivery-messaging-cx.md CX-07 carries the same ratification: 'The parent row projects `Partial acceptance` while evidence is mixed.'
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a partially-accepted delivery has a board representation at all. An implementer reading 12.02.03 alone builds no projection for it and no projection for a transport failure.
findings.notes: Lower severity than #003 because following the cross-reference resolves it — but the stale side asserts an absence rather than pointing at the resolution.

findings.claim: Two features route blocking conditions to the Delivery Readiness Gate that the gate's condition taxonomy — which declares itself exhaustive — does not contain, and which the gate's own precondition rule makes unreachable (a blocking validation finding un-presents the gate rather than showing anything on it).
findings.evidence: 12.01.03-delivery-readiness-gate.md:56-57 '**Conditions** are the gate\'s own: social checks over facts other humans own. These are enumerated exhaustively below.' — the five families A–E that follow contain no condition for a missing (P)/(C) year, a missing 09 ownership record, or absent territory data. Against 12.01.05-label-copy-distributor-of-record.md:82 '| No release year available yet | (P)/(C) year cannot derive; field left empty and flagged at the readiness gate (12.01.03) |' and :92 '| Empty | No ownership record in 09 | Blocking — routes to the readiness gate (12.01.03) rather than asking for free text here |'; and 12.03.01-store-selection-territory-scoping.md:255 '| Rights record has no territory data at all | **Cannot derive.** Blocks, routes to the gate (12.01.03). Never defaults to worldwide (D-04) |'. The gate's own P-1 rule (:52) means a release with a blocking validation finding is in the 'Not presented' state (:249), so nothing can be 'flagged at the readiness gate'.
findings.forcedInvention: Where each of these three conditions is actually enforced — as a 12.01.02 blocking validation finding (gate not presented), as a new gate condition family (gate presented and blocked), or at store selection. The artist-visible difference is which screen stops them and what it says.
findings.notes: 12.01.03 Family E covers '02 or 09 unreachable' — a service failure — not 'the record exists and is empty', which is what 12.01.05 and 12.03.01 send it.

findings.claim: 12.04.03 ratifies 'Pre-saves survive a release date change' as a decision, while the sub-domain CX file records that the grant lives at the DSP, that survival is the store's behaviour rather than the platform's decision, and that the decision 'may be an intention we cannot actually honour' — unresolved, with no owner and an expired deferral target.
findings.evidence: 12.04.03-pre-save-pre-add-links.md:107 '| D-04 | Pre-saves survive a release date change | A date move is not the fan\'s fault |' and its edge case at :64 '| Release date moves | Pre-saves must survive it | Must hold — a date move that dropped every pre-save would be catastrophic and is not the fan\'s fault |'. Against 12.04-release-scheduling-windows-cx.md:80 'The pre-save grant lives at the DSP, not with us — we cannot re-point what we do not hold. Whether a store\'s pre-save survives a date change is **the store\'s behaviour, not our decision**, which means D-04 in 12.04.03 ("pre-saves survive a date change") may be an intention we cannot actually honour. That needs confirming per store before it is stated to artists. `[PENDING — Step 5]`' and the map row at :14 'per-store behaviour on date change is `[PENDING — Step 5]`'. 12.04.01-release-date-lead-time.md:289 corroborates the doubt from the other side: 'Pulling this forward risks every pre-save on Spotify firing against a record that isn\'t there yet. We can\'t undo that for your fans.'
findings.forcedInvention: What the platform does to existing pre-saves on a date change (re-point, re-issue, or nothing), and — the product half — whether the artist is told pre-saves are safe when the platform cannot make that true on every store. None of 12.04.03's three open questions covers it.
findings.notes: The `[PENDING — Step 5]` target has passed (the tree is at Step 6 depth), and the marker carries no owner.

findings.claim: Whether a claim-resolving update (attaching a clearance, adding the missed credit) is permitted while a release is suspended is left unresolved with no owner and no deferral target, while 12.05.02 specifies a blanket block that the CX file says defeats the resolution the suspension is waiting for.
findings.evidence: 12.05.02-metadata-update-redelivery.md:102 '| Involuntary takedown active (12.05.03) | Updates blocked while unresolved | "This release is suspended. Fix the dispute first." |' and the state at :118 '| Blocked | Involuntary takedown active | Suspended, with the route to contest |'. Against 12.05-catalog-lifecycle-after-release-cx.md:13 'Back-edge: an update can *resolve* a claim (adding the missed credit, attaching the clearance) — which is exactly what CX-01 blocks … whether a resolving update is permitted during suspension is unresolved' and :80 'Leaning: allow **additive evidence** (clearances, credits, attestations) during suspension; block **mutations** of the claimed facts. That distinction is worth carrying to Step 5.' CX-01 §1 frames the consequence: 'the product has locked them in a room and told them the key is inside.' None of 12.05.03's three open questions (Q-01 posture, Q-02 statutory, Q-03 freeze-vs-takedown) covers it.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the suspension gate is a blanket freeze on all edits or an additive-evidence carve-out, and — if a carve-out — what classifies an update as additive rather than a mutation of the claimed facts.
findings.notes: A default exists (blanket block), so an implementer can proceed; but the sub-domain records that default as producing a trap, with a stated leaning that was never ratified.

findings.claim: When a metadata update decomposes into takedown + redelivery on a store and fails between the two halves, the release is down and not back up — described as the worst outcome available in the sub-domain — and the recovery behaviour is deferred to a stage that has already run, with no owner and no state for it in 12.05.02.
findings.evidence: 12.05-catalog-lifecycle-after-release-cx.md:62 'An update that decomposes into takedown+redeliver must be atomic in intent — a failure between the two halves leaves the release down and not back up, which is the worst outcome available in this sub-domain.' and :63 'The second path can fail halfway. Recovery is `[PENDING — Step 5]` and matters more than its obscurity suggests.' 12.05.02-metadata-update-redelivery.md's state table (:110-119) offers Live / Costing / Updating / Updated / Partial / Rejected / Blocked / Requested — none of which represents a half-completed decomposition, and its edge-case table has no row for it.
findings.forcedInvention: What the platform does and what the artist sees when the takedown half of a decomposing update succeeds and the redelivery half fails: automatic retry, a distinct 'down, not restored' state, or a manual recovery route.
findings.notes: 12.05-cx CX-03 §3 also records that a Producer holding only `Config` on updates can, through this decomposition, effect a takedown they have `Read-only` on — the permission consequence of the same unspecified path.
